mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let’s bring all this together. Moving from perfectionism to bravery isn’t some perfect journey—it's a series of choices, day in and day out. Sometimes they're big, sometimes they're tiny. But each one matters. What you’ll notice is, bravery isn’t about waiting until you’re not scared anymore. It grows with practice—by choosing courage, even when fear, or the urge to please, tries to take the wheel. So if you’re ready to start living a little braver, here are a few gentle reminders to carry with you: Bravery gets stronger the more you use it. Don’t wait for fear to vanish. Mistakes? They’re not proof you can’t do it—they’re the stepping stones that get you there. Be kind to yourself. Self-compassion quiets that loud, inner critic. And remember, you don’t have to go it alone. Community can turn courage from something you carry by yourself into something you share. Maybe the most powerful thing? The next generation is watching you. They learn how to be brave by seeing you try, fall, and get back up. So, you don’t have to be fearless. You don’t need the whole plan mapped out. What the world really needs is for you to show up, speak up, and let yourself be seen. Every small act of courage, every moment you choose to be real, makes life just a little brighter—and a little kinder—for all of us. Take a deep breath. Let go of getting it all right. Try something new, even if you’re not sure what’ll happen. Ask for help when you need it. Cheer someone else on when you can. Celebrate the effort, not just the finish line. And when you stumble—and you will—remind yourself, you’re not alone. Bravery isn’t about never falling. It’s about getting back up, again and again. The path to a bolder, more authentic life? It’s wide open. All it really takes is one brave step at a time.
